problems.title: The square root is always nonnegative
problems.question: Simplify √((-x)²) for real x.
problems.idea: A square root does not restore an unknown sign.
steps: The result is |-x|=|x|, equal to x for x≥0 and -x for x<0.

problems.title: Simplify radicals before multiplying
problems.question: Evaluate (√72-√48)(√8+√27)/(2√6).
problems.idea: Extract perfect-square factors.

problems.title: Equal circles and their common chord
problems.question: Two equal circles have common chord length 6 cm. Their overlap segment along the line of centres is 2 cm. Find the radius.
problems.idea: The common chord lies halfway between the centres.

problems.title: A linear inequality with fractions
problems.question: Solve 3-3x/2>5/8-(4x-3)/6.
problems.idea: Clear denominators with positive 24.
formulas: Multiplication by a positive number preserves the inequality.

problems.title: The printed geometry does not match its choices
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, BK⊥AC with BK=4 cm. K is 1 cm from side AD. Find AK.
problems.idea: Use the projection of AK along AB, retaining both length conditions.
formulas: Projection theorem in right ABK: AK²=AB·projection of AK onto AB; AB²=AK²+BK².
steps: The perpendicular distance from K to AD equals that projection, namely 1. Hence if t=AK, AB=t².
Pythagoras gives t⁴=t²+16. Put u=t²>0; then u²-u-16=0, so u=(1+√65)/2.
problems.note: None of the listed simple lengths equals the value forced by BK=4 and the 1 cm distance. The data have been used as printed.

problems.title: Exactly seven integer points in an open interval
problems.question: Find p so |x|<p-1 has exactly seven integer solutions.
problems.idea: The solutions must be -3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3.
formulas: To include ±3 require p-1>3; to exclude ±4 require p-1≤4.

problems.title: Count similar-triangle pairs in the drawn figure
problems.question: In the drawn 36°-apex isosceles triangle, AD is the A-bisector and O the incentre. Count pairs of similar triangles formed by the drawn segments.
problems.idea: Group triangles by their angle triples.
formulas: Triangles are similar iff their corresponding angles agree; k triangles give C(k,2) pairs.
steps: The drawn triangles ABC,ACD,COD all have angles 36°,72°,72°. They give C(3,2)=3 pairs.
Triangles ABD,AOC both have angles 36°,36°,108°, giving one further pair.
These five are the triangles formed by the drawn segments, so the total is 4.

problems.title: Three equal pieces of a trapezoid midline
problems.question: A trapezoid midline is split into three equal parts by its diagonals. In what ratio does the diagonal intersection divide a diagonal?
problems.idea: The outer midline pieces are half the short base.
formulas: Midline pieces are b/2,(B-b)/2,b/2; diagonal division ratio=B:b.
steps: Therefore the diagonal division ratio is 2:1, or 1:2 when read in the opposite direction.

problems.title: A smaller isosceles triangle inside the original
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base 6 and legs 8. M,N are on the legs with AM:MN:NC=2:3:2. Find perimeter BMN.
problems.idea: Equal removed side lengths make MN parallel to the base.
steps: BM=BN=16/3 and MN=4. Their sum is 44/3.

problems.title: A parallel line gives a simple ratio
problems.question: BM:MC=1:3 and AN:NC=3:2. MT∥BN, with T on AC. Find CT:AN.
problems.idea: Triangles CMT,CBN are similar.

problems.title: Mass points for intersecting cevians
problems.question: BM:MC=1:3,AN:NC=3:2, and AM,BN meet at K. Find AK:KM.
problems.idea: Assign vertex masses that balance each division.
steps: Then the mass at M is 12.

problems.title: Intersecting two linear half-lines
problems.question: Which cannot be the solution set of ax≤b,cx≥d with ab≠0: empty,ℝ,closed interval,left half-line,a single point?
problems.idea: The first inequality already confines x to a proper half-line.
formulas: If a≠0, ax≤b is a proper closed half-line.
steps: Its intersection with any second condition cannot become the whole real line.
The other listed shapes are possible by choosing the second half-line to be disjoint, opposite-facing, redundant, or touching at one endpoint.

problems.title: Convert repeating decimals to fractions
problems.question: Evaluate 0.6(96)+0.33(3), with parentheses denoting repeating digits.
problems.idea: The first is 0.696969… and the second 1/3.

problems.title: The shaded half-plane
problems.question: Identify the inequality shown by the solid rising boundary through (-2,0),(0,3), shaded below.
problems.idea: Find the boundary equation, then choose its lower side.
steps: Below it means y≤3x/2+3. Multiply by 2 to get 2y-3x≤6.

problems.title: Use a defining quadratic to simplify a ratio
problems.question: Find (a²+3a)/(8a-18) if a²+7a-9=0.
problems.idea: Replace a² with 9-7a.
steps: The numerator is -1/2 times the denominator.
The denominator is not zero at a root: a=9/4 would not satisfy the given quadratic.
Therefore the ratio is -1/2 for both roots.

problems.title: Two secants from one exterior point
problems.question: One secant has external length 5 cm and internal length 15 cm. A second has equal external and internal lengths. Find its whole length.
problems.idea: Use the power-of-a-point product.
formulas: External·whole is the same for both secants.
steps: If each second-secant part is t, t·2t=100, giving t=5√2.

problems.title: Extract a factor with the correct sign
problems.question: Simplify √(-m³) over the reals.
problems.idea: The domain determines the sign of m.

problems.title: Axis distances require absolute values
problems.question: For M=(a-4,a+1), distance to the x-axis is half its distance to the y-axis. Find a.
problems.idea: Use the absolute coordinates as distances.
steps: Both satisfy the original absolute-value equation.

problems.title: Radicals of squares on a stated interval
problems.question: Simplify √(x²-18x+81)+√(x²+4x+4) for 1<x<8.
problems.idea: Replace square roots of squares with absolute values.
steps: On this interval x-9<0 and x+2>0.

problems.title: Hay after half the horses leave
problems.question: Hay feeds 10 horses for 15 days. After 2 days, 5 leave. For how many more days does it feed the remaining horses?
problems.idea: Count horse-days of remaining stock.

problems.title: Two radical-equation roots
problems.question: Find the sum of squared roots of √(-x-1)+x+1=0.
steps: The equation becomes t-t²=0, giving t=0 or 1.
The corresponding x are -1 and -2, both valid.

problems.title: Centroids form a parallelogram
problems.question: In convex ABCD, O is the diagonal intersection. Find the perimeter of the quadrilateral formed by the centroids of AOB,BOC,COD,DOA if AC=12,BD=18.
problems.idea: Subtract adjacent centroid vectors.
steps: Adjacent centroid differences are (C-A)/3 and (D-B)/3, repeated with opposite signs.
Thus the new quadrilateral has side lengths AC/3=4 and BD/3=6.

problems.title: A positive denominator factor controls a parameter inequality
problems.question: Solve (ax+b)/(a-b)>(ax+b)/(a+b), with a>b>0.
problems.idea: Subtract the two sides.
steps: Thus the inequality is equivalent to ax+b>0.

problems.title: A negative numerator forces a negative denominator
problems.question: If (2√2-3)/[1-(1-√2)p]>0, locate p+√2.
problems.idea: The numerator is negative because 8<9.
formulas: A positive quotient with negative numerator requires negative denominator.

problems.title: Scale a right-triangle perimeter
problems.question: From acute vertex A of parallelogram ABCD drop AM⊥BC and AN⊥CD, to the lines. Given perimeter ABM=7.2 and AB:BC=2:3, find perimeter AMCN.
problems.idea: Express both perimeters with the same trigonometric factor.
formulas: Let AB=s,BC=t,A=θ; projections are s cosθ,t cosθ and heights s sinθ,t sinθ.
steps: The right triangle ABM has perimeter s(1+sinθ+cosθ)=7.2.
The quadrilateral sides add to (s+t)(1+sinθ+cosθ), including the external projection segments on the two lines.
Since t/s=3/2, multiply by (s+t)/s=5/2 to get 18.
